sanskrit: arasasya śarkoṭasya nīcīnasyopasarpataḥ | viṣaṃ hi sarvam ādiṣy atho enam ajījabham ||
english: Of the virulence-stripped scorpion that crawls downward and approaches — I have consumed all its venom; moreover I have silenced it.

sanskrit: na te bāhvo raso asti na śīrṣe nota madhyataḥ | kim idaṃ pāpayāmuyā pucche bibharṣy arbhakam ||
english: There is no potency in your claws, none in your head, nor yet in your middle. What then is this wretched little thing you carry in your tail?

sanskrit: yat te skandhān upatasthau vijāmni yac ca te parau | apamityam ivābhṛtaṃ malaṃ te prati dadhmasi ||
english: Whatever poison has settled in your shoulders, in the joint-spaces, and whatever is in your feet — we blow that defilement back at you, as one returns a borrowed debt.

sanskrit: adanti tvā pipīlikā vi vṛścanti mayūryaḥ | sarve bhala bravātha śārkoṭam arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: The ants devour you; the peahens tear you apart. Declare it well, all of you: the scorpion's venom is rendered powerless!

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ me dakṣiṇe haste savye me jaya āhitaḥ | gojid bhūyāsam aśvajit kṛtaṃcayo hiraṇyajit ||
english: The winning throw is placed in my right hand; victory is set in my left. May I be a winner of cattle, a winner of horses — one who amasses winnings, a winner of gold.

sanskrit: akṣāḥ phalavatīṃ divaṃ datta gāṃ kṣīriṇīm iva | saṃ mā kṛtasya dhārayā dhanuḥ snāvneva nahyata ||
english: O dice, give me a fruit-bearing heaven, like a cow rich with milk. Bind me with the stream of the winning throw, as a bow is bound with its sinew.

sanskrit: ubhau hastau pratidīvno brahmaṇāpombhāmasi | kalir enaṃ yathā hanad āsya vedo bharāmahai ||
english: Both hands of my adversary in dicing we smite with the brahman-power — so that the Kali throw may strike him down; we shall carry off his wealth.

sanskrit: ā bhadraṃ dvāparam uta tretāṃ parā kalim | kṛtaṃ me hasta āhitaṃ sa hi saumanaso mahān ||
english: Hither the Bhadra, hither the Dvāpara, and the Tretā — away with the Kali! The winning throw is placed in my hand; for it is the great one that brings good cheer.

sanskrit: yad eyatha pareyatha yat te tan mana īyate | tatas tvā punar arvāñcaṃ bhūtasyājīgamat patiḥ ||
english: Wheresoever you roam to and fro, wheresoever your mind wanders — from that place may the Lord of beings cause you to come back hither again.

sanskrit: ā tvā nayād bhūtapatir ā devo bṛhaspatiḥ | ādityāḥ sarve tvā neṣan viśve devāḥ suvarcasaḥ ||
english: May Bhūtapati lead you back; may the god Bṛhaspati lead you back; may all the Ādityas conduct you hither; may the All-Gods, resplendent in glory, bring you back.

sanskrit: anumatiḥ sarasvatī bhago rājā ny ā nayāt | śālā mānasya patnī- -ihaivāsya manas karat ||
english: May Anumati, may Sarasvatī, may King Bhaga lead him back home. The house — the wife of the heart — may it here and now make his mind settle.

sanskrit: yas tvā ninānayakaḥ sa u tvehā nayāt punaḥ | mano hi brahmāṇo vidur viśvakarmā manīṣiṇaḥ ||
english: He who once led you away — may that same one lead you back hither again. For the brahmins know the mind; Viśvakarmā, the wise one, knows it.
